stories.headline: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills at least 12; Saudi Arabia threatens a decisive response

sources.body:
At least 12 people have been killed and 309 injured in an attack on the international airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, local authorities say.

The deaths included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed.

Operations at King Khalid International Airport have been suspended after the attack, which was the deadliest in the kingdom since May 2015.

A Saudi-led military coalition later vowed to respond to the attack, which it called a "war crime" and blamed on Yemen's Houthis.

The Houthis have not commented on Saturday's attack but did say they were behind strikes on the same airport on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane.

Another three people were killed in separate Houthi attacks on two different Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October.

Fighting has recently escalated between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who are backed by Iran and control most of the country.

As well as the strikes on Riyadh's airport, a projectile also fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam in eastern Saudi Arabia on Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition said.

In Saturday's statement, the Saudi civil aviation authority said some of the injured were "in critical condition" and damage to the airport was being assessed.

More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, an eyewitness told the Reuters news agency.

Saudi-led coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki later said the attack on one of the passenger terminals resulted in deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport staff.

He described the attack as a "full-fledged war crime".

An eyewitness told Reuters they had seen "injured [people] in front of my eyes" fleeing from gate 401 after it was hit.

António Guterres, Secretary General of the United Nations, said he was "deeply shocked" by the attacks which he called a "violation of international law" that "must cease immediately".

In a statement on X, Kuwait's foreign ministry called the strikes a "heinous and cowardly attack". The attacks were also condemned by Egypt, Palestine and Qatar.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio strongly condemned recent attacks on Saudi Arabia as he confirmed an American citizen was killed in the strikes.

Speaking to reporters, US President Donald Trump indicated he may join the Saudis in carrying out strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis.

"We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."

For the second time in less than a month, schools in Riyadh have switched to remote learning for the week.

Western embassies in Saudi Arabia warned their citizens to stay away from the Riyadh airport. The UK Foreign Office told British nationals to avoid the area "until the airport is secure". The US embassy has told staff they must seek "special authorisation" to use the airports in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam.

Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there.
sources.headline: Twelve killed and 300 injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh

sources.body:
Donald Trump evaluating whether US should join Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Yemeni rebels

The latest attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital of Riyadh killed 12 people and injured more than 300 others, civil aviation authorities said early on Sunday, with some in a critical condition. A Saudi-led coalition blamed Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen.

A missile struck a King Khalid international airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorised to speak to the media.

A Saudi statement said the dead included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said the injured were being treated at several hospitals.

The US president, Donald Trump, said he was evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen . “We may. We’re going to look at it,” Trump said. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.”

The US secretary of ⁠state, Marco ⁠Rubio, called the attacks “​reprehensible” and said “they must ​stop ‌now”.

One witness at the Riyadh airport reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded.

“I was on gate 403,” at the domestic terminal, the witness told the Agence France-Presse news agency. “I saw [gate] 401 hit, I saw injured [people] in front of my eyes. Everyone was running.”

The relative of one injured person said they had been wounded in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass and taken to hospital.

A projectile also fell near the King Fahd international airport in Dammam, according to the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis . The Dammam airport has become an important alternative to Riyadh amid the recent spate of attacks.

There was no immediate statement from the rebels, who earlier Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sana’a international airport in the Houthi-held Yemeni capital.

Schools in Riyadh will move to remote learning for a week, according to the education ministry, following the deadly attack.

Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis ⁠on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this ​week, leaving four people dead and ‌others wounded, and ‌badly damaging an aircraft.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.

The attack came as forces allied to the UN-recognised government in Yemen claim to have mounted a successful offensive to retake the Bab al-Mandab strait from Houthi rebels, but accounts vary as to whether the push has been repelled.

A Houthi spokesperson said forces from the Saudi-backed government based in Aden “were targeted with a large number of ballistic missiles, artillery support and heavy weapons, resulting in the destruction of more than 22 armoured vehicles and the killing and wounding of dozens, including a number of commanders.
sources.headline: Twelve killed and hundreds injured in Houthi attack at Riyadh airport

sources.body: Saudi Arabia vowed to retaliate against Yemen’s Houthi rebels on Sunday after a strike on Riyadh’s international airport killed a dozen people and wounded more than 300, marking the kingdom's deadliest strike in a decade.
sources.headline: Saudi Arabia threatens 'decisive' response after Riyadh airport strike kills at least 12

stories.headline: Trump calls for Ukraine to replace Zelenskyy amid dispute over Russian diesel and refinery strikes

sources.body:
US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.

The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.

"He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal".

Since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022 the country has been under martial law, meaning elections are suspended.

Global fuel supplies, including diesel, have been severely limited by the war against Iran launched by the US and Israel, which led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil products usually flows.

Russia - a major producer - and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes on each other's energy infrastructure and transport facilities, further straining energy markets.

"We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," Trump continued.

"He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does."

Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace".

The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April.

Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.

He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia.

The Ukrainian president spoke to several allies on Saturday to discuss the latest developments, calling for "real decisions to protect lives in Ukraine" and to protect European security.

A Downing Street spokesperson said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham had spoken to Zelensky and offered his "complete solidarity".

The pair had agreed Russia should acquiesce to "an immediate energy ceasefire" and end its attacks on shipping in the Black Sea, the spokesperson said, as "this would immediately release more energy and food supplies into the global market".

News of the US-Russia diesel deal was also met with criticism by EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas, who echoed Zelensky in saying that suspending sanctions "provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war", adding: "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't."

She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday.
sources.headline: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal

sources.body:
US president suggests Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has not done enough to end war

Donald Trump has said Ukraine needs “a new leader”, a day after making a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy large quantities of Russian diesel.

The US president suggested Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war with Russia and blamed him for high diesel prices in the US.

“I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does,” Trump said.

Trump made the comments as Russia launched deadly strikes on civilians in Ukraine , which Zelenskyy said were a “thanks” to Trump for the diesel deal.

The Ukrainian president has expressed outrage at the agreement announced by Trump on Friday, which the US president said was needed to reduce diesel prices, and comes ahead of November’s midterm elections in which fuel costs are a key voter issue.

The deal, which appeared to blindside Kyiv as it was announced while Ukrainian negotiators were in Miami for peace talks, was described by Zelenskyy as a “gift” to Russia’s president.

He said Russia would use the money it raised from the fuel sales to invest in its war and that “any easing of sanctions” would play into Russia’s hands, “allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer”.

That prediction was realised hours later, when Ukrainian officials announced that a barrage of Russian strikes on the country’s south-east early on Saturday had killed 20 people, including three children.

“Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelenskyy said on social media on Saturday.

“Last night confirmed once again that in Russia, they take any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed,” he said.

There were also “large-scale power outages” in the capital, Kyiv, the country’s largest private energy provider said.

Andy Burnham reiterated his “complete solidarity” in a call with Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the leaders agreed to meet in person in the coming days to continue talks.

The prime minister said he recognised the past day had been “difficult for Ukraine” and the two talked about the importance of keeping up pressure on Russia, No 10 said.

In stark contrast to Zelenskyy’s open frustration with Trump, a Kremlin readout of Friday’s call between the US president and Putin was glowing, with the Russian ⁠news agency Interfax ⁠quoting ​an aide as saying it was “very substantive and friendly”.

“Neither wanted to be the first to hang up,” the Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said of the two leaders. “They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time.” ​ Zelenskyy has previously said Putin is playing games with Trump.

The diesel deal disrupts four years of western financial pressure on Moscow and leaves Kyiv’s allies in Europe and Nato scrambling to adapt their sanctions plan. The EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the diesel deal “provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war”.
sources.headline: Trump says Ukraine needs a new leader after diesel deal with Russia

sources.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Sunday said Kyiv was ready halt strikes Russian oil refineries if Moscow stopped attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. The announcement comes after US President Donald Trump publicly urged him to stop targeting Russian refineries.
sources.headline: Ukraine ready to halt refinery strikes if Moscow stops energy attacks, Zelensky says

stories.headline: Iran war disrupts global energy supplies as conflict deepens economic strain

sources.body:
Fossil fuels produce 81 percent of global energy. We look at the Middle East’s role and what happens when supplies are cut.

A major energy conference is going ahead in Riyadh from Sunday despite a Houthi attack on the city’s King Khalid International Airport that killed 12 people and injured 309, according to Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation.

Saudi ⁠Arabia’s Ministry of Energy said on Sunday that the 25th ⁠World Petroleum Council Energy Congress has begun ‌in Riyadh. The 17th International Energy Forum (IEF) Ministerial will be held on the sidelines of the conference, called Riyadh Energy Week, which is to run until Thursday.

But Italy, the cohost of the IEF, will join the meeting via videolink. Nigeria, the other cohost, is sending a representative to the event.

The IEF brings together 68 countries that account for more than 90 percent of global oil and gas supplies and demand. Its members include Saudi Arabia, the United States and Russia. The meeting comes as the US-Israel war on Iran has disrupted energy flows and pushed governments to reassess their energy security.

In this visual explainer, Al Jazeera looks at where the world’s energy comes from, how much is produced in the Middle East and which countries have strategic reserves to fall back on.

Energy heats our homes, fuels our cars, keeps the lights on and runs the factories that make what we buy. It comes from fossil fuels such as oil, coal and gas as well as nuclear power and renewables.

Despite rapid growth in renewables, fossil fuels still account for nearly 81 percent of global energy consumption. Oil is the largest source at 31.4 percent, followed by coal at 25.9 percent and natural gas at 23.5 percent. Traditional biomass, nuclear power and other sources make up the rest.

Production is concentrated in a handful of regions, so disruptions in any of them ripple through global markets.

The Middle East is the largest oil-producing region, and North America is the largest natural gas producer. Russia and Central Asia are also major producers of both.

The Middle East’s importance to energy markets is also about geography. Three narrow waterways connect its producers with consumers around the world.

Before the Iran war, about 27 percent of global seaborne oil trade and almost 20 percent of liquefied natural gas trade transited through the Strait of Hormuz on the eastern side of the Arabian Peninsula.

On the peninsula’s western side, the Bab al-Mandeb strait links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, and the Suez Canal connects the Red Sea with the Mediterranean. As the Iran war has spilled over into other areas of the Middle East and Yemen’s civil war has ramped up, traffic has been reduced through both the strait and canal, forcing some energy shipments on longer routes around Africa.

“That’s probably the first time we’ve really seen a major constriction of a chokepoint,” said Richard Matthews, director of consultancy and research at Gibson Shipbrokers, a London-based shipbroking and maritime advisory service.
sources.headline: What the Iran war has done to the world’s energy supply, in charts

sources.body: Iran's economy has been battered by years of sanctions, but the conflict that began in February with US-Israeli attacks and an American blockade of the country's ports has put extra strain on daily life. Rising inflation, nearly 90 percent year-on-year in September according to official figures, and erratic currency exchange fluctuations have driven up the cost of everyday items. Food prices have more than doubled since last year.
sources.headline: 'Going bankrupt': Iran shopkeepers struggle as war dims demand

stories.headline: Pakistan imposes emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, governed by Imran Khan's party

sources.body:
PM’s office says cabinet move follows ‘provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’.

Authorities in Pakistan have announced a state of emergency in the northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

The state of emergency was invoked on Sunday under two articles of the constitution dealing with security. It effectively suspends the provincial government run by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of jailed former Prime ⁠Minister Imran Khan.

President Asif Ali Zardari said in a social media post he had approved the recommendations made by the cabinet, which had held a meeting under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif earlier in the day.

A statement issued by Sharif’s office said cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.

Pakistan’s constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions ⁠during an emergency, though the president’s office did not specify how the province would ⁠be administered.

Shortly after the announcement, PTI lawmaker Junaid Akbar said Sohail Afridi, the chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, was arrested along with the party’s president in the province.

The move comes as the PTI has been preparing for a march on the capital , Islamabad, to demand the release of Khan, who has been in jail for more than three years but still commands widespread popularity across the country.

The march was originally scheduled for September 27 but was postponed until October 4 to allow talks between the government and the PTI leadership to take place.

The government, however, said it would not allow the march to enter the capital and has been preparing for weeks to prevent the arrival of PTI demonstrators in Islamabad. It has erected barriers using shipping containers to block main access routes to the capital.

PTI spokesman Zulfikar Bukhari said the decision to invoke the state of emergency would only lead to “further bloodshed, ‌instability and collateral damage”, the Reuters news agency reported.

He said there was room for talks, but the latest decision showed the government never intended to hold negotiations.
sources.headline: Pakistan imposes emergency rule in ​province governed by Imran Khan’s party

stories.headline: Ebola spreads in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as Kenya confirms an imported case

sources.body:
New cases in eastern DRC and a fatal imported infection in Kenya highlight the challenges of containing Ebola.

Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo – The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has spread to another health zone in the east, while a fatal imported case in Kenya has underscored the risk of cross-border transmission.

The World Health Organization (WHO) said in an October 8 update that Alimbongo health zone in North Kivu province had reported cases for the first time. As of October 6, four confirmed cases, including two deaths, had been recorded there.

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a species of Ebola virus. According to the WHO, cases had been reported in 64 health zones across seven provinces in the DRC. Ituri remained the worst-affected province in cumulative cases, while North Kivu was accounting for a growing share of newly confirmed infections.

As of October 6, the WHO had recorded 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 confirmed deaths in the DRC. A further 2,269 people had recovered, and the crude case fatality ratio stood at 48.2 percent.

Kenya confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease on October 6, according to the WHO. The patient, a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the DRC, fell ill there and received treatment at several health facilities before travelling to Kenya through Uganda.

The patient travelled by road to Kampala, Uganda, before flying to Nairobi, arriving on October 3. The patient was isolated in hospital and tested positive for the virus. Despite supportive treatment, the patient died on October 5, the WHO said.

Kenyan authorities identified 28 contacts, including family members and healthcare workers. The WHO also reported efforts to trace passengers and crew members from the flight to Nairobi.

Public health measures have been initiated in Kenya and Uganda, including contact tracing and enhanced surveillance.

On October 8, preliminary laboratory results for a suspected Ebola case in Kenya’s Wajir County came back negative, according to the county governor. The result eased concerns about a possible second case, although monitoring continued.

The imported infection has underscored the importance of surveillance and coordination between neighbouring countries. Identifying exposed people and monitoring them for symptoms are central to detecting infections early and interrupting further transmission.

In the DRC, the response is facing mounting pressure from limited treatment capacity, insecurity and difficulties securing cooperation from some communities.

Daniel Makasi Levergénois, founder of Watoto Radio, said insecurity and misinformation were undermining efforts to contain the outbreak. In Beni and Butembo, both in North Kivu, rumours and misconceptions about Ebola had contributed to reluctance among some residents to cooperate with response teams, he said.

In an October 5 update, medical charity Doctors Without Borders, known by its French initials MSF, said North Kivu accounted for nearly 40 percent of newly confirmed cases nationwide, up from 24 percent at the end of August.
sources.headline: Ebola spreads in eastern DRC as Kenya confirms imported case

Pope Leo XIV says he will undergo surgery for an early-stage lung nodule

sources.body:
Pope Leo XIV has announced he will be operated "in the coming days" after a nodule was found on his lung during a medical check up.

"The doctors found an early, well-localised nodule on my lung," he told the public during his weekly Sunday prayers in St Peter's Square in Rome.

The 71-year-old pontiff said his medical team "believe it would be right to intervene" and he had agreed to the operation.

Pope Leo reassured pilgrims that the mass was "well-contained" and caught "at an early stage".

He concluded his Angelus prayer by thanking everyone for their "spiritual closeness" and said he entrusted himself to their prayers.

Holy See Press Office spokesperson Matteo Bruni told the media that "the operation is scheduled for the first days of next week".

Bruni added that the Pope is expected to take about a week to recover.

Pope Leo, born Robert Francis Provost, succeeded Pope Francis in 2025. He is the 267th occupant of the throne of St Peter – and the first American.

He was ordained in 1982 and spent years as a missionary in Peru, where he is remembered as a figure who worked with marginalised communities and helped build bridges.
sources.headline: Pope Leo to have surgery after lump found on lung

stories.headline: Republican changes to SNAP food assistance become a midterm issue as states absorb new costs

sources.body: Under the political radar, the country’s food stamps program is undergoing a slow-motion transformation. The ramifications could bubble up into the midterms. Changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program from Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act are rolling out in phases, from tougher work requirements to restrictions on non-citizens. Food stamp rolls already shrank by more than 5 million people nationwide as of this summer, as the hardest-hit state, Arizona, saw an outright majority of its food stamp recipients lose benefits. The latest alteration clicked into place Oct. 1, when the share of administrative costs states and counties have to pay rose to 75% from 50%. An even bigger financial shift looms in a year, when states with high payment error rates will have to assume some benefit costs for the first time, a scenario that’s already rippling through state and local budget planning. It all adds up to a new era in federal-state relations — and in the size and nature of the welfare state. In a year when affordability worries top voters’ priority lists and grocery prices strain their wallets, Democrats think the SNAP shift gives them an opening to make Republicans pay politically after the GOP used social safety net cuts to food aid and Medicaid to help pay for last year’s tax cuts. “People are getting kicked off these programs at the very moment they’re going to the polls to vote,” House Agriculture ranking member Angie Craig (D-Minn.) said. “I sure wouldn’t want to be a Republican headed into the November ballot.” But Republicans think they have a compelling story to tell voters, trying to right-size a program that spends millions of dollars on erroneous payments. The SNAP changes align with the Trump administration’s broader push to crack down on fraud and make the government smaller or more efficient. Implementing stricter work requirements for welfare often polls well, and trying to move people toward work gets at the root causes of poverty, they argue. “The premise is simple: Let’s make sure that this program is preserved for those truly in need, and that we aren’t squandering taxpayer dollars,” a senior USDA official told Playbook in an interview. “And let’s make sure that if folks are able-bodied, they are work training or volunteering for 20 hours per week.” That doesn’t mean Republicans in competitive races are putting SNAP and Medicaid cuts front and center on the campaign trail. When they tout last year’s megalaw, new tax breaks typically lead the messaging. And 10 frontline GOP House campaigns didn’t respond to requests for interviews about how they can win on SNAP. At the state and county level, some governments are scrambling to prepare for a massive cost shift, hitting at the same time as significant Medicaid changes. The resulting bureaucratic jumble has contributed to some of the SNAP losses this year, as recipients struggled to get through overtaxed call centers, some states cut staff, and others tightened their processes. “It really sets up a change in the federal responsibility, and I view it as a slippery slope,” warned Barbara Guinn, New York’s commissioner of the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance. Her state is staring down a possible $1 billion added burden next year, though they’re advocating for a repeal of the benefits change. “Once they implement any kind of cost shift, I think it will be easier for them to take similar actions in the future.” Whether to delay next year’s cost shift has already generated tensions over the farm bill in the Senate, where Democrats are demanding a longer postponement than Republicans’ offer of one year. Some Minnesota counties are considering significant property tax increases to pay for the extra costs, Craig said: “We’re going to be pushing hard for a two-year delay — at the request of, frankly, many of my Republican county commissioners, not just Democrats.” Conservatives see the new calculus as a long overdue change to improve efficiency and incentivize program integrity. Improper payment rates are high in many states (though they comprise both over-payments and under-payments, and error rates are different from fraud). Those that reduce errors enough won’t have to take on paying the benefits. And even opponents of the changes think lower error rates are a worthy goal. SNAP rolls often ebb and flow with the economy, and the recent drop could reflect the job market pulling people out of need — or the removal of people who shouldn’t have been getting food stamps in the first place. “There needs to be some level of accountability,” the USDA official said. States with high error rates “need to start to have skin in the game.” But at a time when many households are already squeezed by inflation, the SNAP changes have correlated with higher numbers of Americans turning to charities to ward off hunger. The surge in people losing food aid came more quickly than expected. The unemployment rate hasn’t meaningfully changed. And the vast majority of large food banks in a recent NBC survey said they were grappling with higher demand, in part due to food stamp changes. Another rule kicking in the day after the midterms could lead to many retailers being bumped out of SNAP as places where low-income people can use their benefits. For state governments, a set of sweeping operational changes are now underway to conform to new policy demands, often requiring more money or staffing at already under-resourced offices. And the budgetary stakes to get error rates lower are sky-high. “It’s a really complicated, nuanced and confusing time for states who are trying to administer SNAP,” said Lauren Kallins, a senior legislative director at the nonpartisan National Conference of State Legislatures, which has advocated for a delay in the benefits costs shift.
sources.headline: Republicans’ SNAP changes land in crunch time for midterms

stories.headline: Democrats are cautioned against complacency in North Carolina's closely watched Senate race

sources.body: National Democrats are increasingly shifting their attention away from North Carolina’s Senate race as polls show former Gov. Roy Cooper ahead, eyeing once long-shot races as possible pickups. But a veteran Democratic strategist who helped deliver the party’s last presidential victory in the state is urging donors not to take a win for granted. David Plouffe, who managed behind Barack Obama’s narrow 2008 victory in North Carolina, urged Democratic donors and supporters not to grow complacent in the final weeks of Roy Cooper’s Senate campaign, according to audio obtained by POLITICO. “I think that this race ... has I think been the best run race in the country,” Plouffe said on the call. “But that doesn't mean that we can rest easy.” He warned about North Carolina’s relatively fixed partisan makeup as a purple state, making it difficult for a candidate to dramatically expand their base of support. “There's certain states that elections happen within a bound, and this one will be that way as well,” he said. In public polling, Cooper leads Republican Michael Whatley, who has struggled to boost his name recognition against the much better-known former governor. And as Democrats grow increasingly bullish on their candidate’s chances of flipping the seat — one of four pickups they need to take control of the Senate — national groups have begun shifting their money and attention to other contests, including most recently to Kansas . But Plouffe said North Carolina needs to remain a priority. “We have to win the ones we have to win,” he said on the call to Cooper’s finance committee. Just days before Plouffe’s remarks, Senate Democrats’ top super PAC pulled back some of its spending in North Carolina, following a much bigger retreat by Republicans’ top super PAC in the state. Plouffe cautioned that North Carolina has historically been a tough state for Democrats at the federal level, especially in recent years. The party hasn’t won a Senate race there since 2008, when Obama became the last Democratic presidential candidate to carry the state, winning by fewer than 15,000 votes. He lost the state in 2012. “Even though we carried the electoral votes back then, we only did so by I think 14,000 votes. So it was our narrowest victory,” Plouffe said. “And in 2012, we tried to win North Carolina again with the help of so many people on this phone, and we just couldn't get it done. And that tells you how difficult the state is.” Plouffe also cast the stakes of Cooper’s race as extending beyond November, arguing that a Cooper victory could provide a blueprint for the party’s eventual 2028 presidential nominee. “Democrats need to compete and win in North Carolina in 28,” he said. “And it's one thing to look how a governor can win a state. The best route, the best scout that you receive, is how someone in a federal race won in a tough state, and that can show you the way.”
sources.headline: David Plouffe warns Dems: Don’t take North Carolina for granted

sources.body: <p>Inés Caballero charlaba con dos amigas en <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-10-10/la-vida-en-la-acampada-de-sol-una-ciudad-espontanea-en-el-corazon-de-madrid-donde-ayuso-dice-que-hay-terrorismo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-10-10/la-vida-en-la-acampada-de-sol-una-ciudad-espontanea-en-el-corazon-de-madrid-donde-ayuso-dice-que-hay-terrorismo.html">la acampada de la Puerta del Sol</a> el jueves pasado. Las tres, sentadas en unas sillas de <i>camping</i>, se encontraban en el centro mismo del laberinto de tiendas que abarrotaba la plaza, protegidas, por un mar de plásticos y lonas, de la lluvia, de las miradas y, hoy, del sol. Inés tiene 28 años, es técnico de teatro en Madrid, el trabajo le gusta, estudió para llegar a él, cobra un sueldo de unos 1.500 euros al mes, goza de contrato fijo y sin embargo, acudió a la llamada de acampar en la Puerta del Sol para protestar. ¿Para protestar por qué? La mujer mira al que le hace la pregunta de frente, esboza un gesto un poco indescifrable y responde: “Buff, por todo. Porque me encuentro en un callejón sin salida. Vivo con mis padres y con este sueldo ahora no puedo comprarme una casa nunca, ni siquiera alquilar yo sola. Por eso me puede la incertidumbre de no saber qué va a ser de mí. ¿Hasta cuándo voy a tener que estar en casa de mis padres? ¿Voy a tener que tener un hijo ahí? Tengo la sensación no de que he fracasado, porque no he fracasado, pero sí de que voy llegando tarde a todo.” A la siguiente pregunta: ¿vas a votar? Responde con un poco más de ánimo: “Pues obviamente. Hay que votar. Entiendo que la gente esté enfadada y frustrada con la política, pero hay que votar”.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-11/el-gran-enfado-salta-a-las-urnas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El gran enfado salta a las urnas

sources.body:
Pedro Sánchez está decidido a dar la batalla en las elecciones de este 29 de noviembre con la vivienda por bandera, prometiendo desplegar políticas que la defiendan "sin fecha de caducidad", y plantando cara a PP y Vox, de quienes ha dicho que "están siempre con la fábula de Pedro y el lobo" y a quienes ha avisado: "El lobo son ellos. Yo en todo caso seré un perro que no tiene amo y, si sirvo a alguien, es a la gente de a pie".

El presidente del Gobierno y secretario general de los socialistas ha arrancado la precampaña en un acto en Dos Hermanas , una localidad sevillana que es ya un talismán electoral para el PSOE. Lo ha hecho rodeado por unas 5.000 personas según el PSOE y acompañado por la secretaria general de los socialistas andaluces, María Jesús Montero, que será una de las responsables de su campaña, y el alcalde de la localidad, Francisco Rodríguez.

Sánchez está decidido a centrar su campaña en la vivienda, que es la que le ha llevado a adelantar las elecciones ante la presión de la calle tras el fracaso inicial de sus dos decretos en el Congreso. Decretos que ha rescatado ya con las Cortes Disueltas en el Consejo de Ministros y que serán sometidos la próxima semana a votación en la Diputación Permanente, donde ya no necesita a Junts. Y todo, con una huelga general motivada por la vivienda a la vista el próximo 11 de noviembre, antes de los comicios.

Al inicio de su intervención, ha trasladado su "respeto y cariño" a Maricarmen, la mujer de 87 años cuyo desahucio hace algo más de dos semanas inició las protestas, y a sus seres queridos. Pero también "a todas las personas que están sufriendo, como ella, los abusos y amenazas de los fondos buitre".

Ha puesto énfasis en su "compromiso" con la vivienda, con dos decretos que, ha recordado, fueron tumbados por PP, Vox y Junts, y rescató después.

"Este es mi compromiso: la política de vivienda no tiene fecha de caducidad y el próximo parlamento, con una amplia mayoría progresista, y el gobierno progresista, reforzarán y mantendrán ese decreto de vivienda que protege a pequeños propietarios e inquilinos de la especulación", ha aseverado.

" Maricarmen y todos los que se están movilizando con ella y por la causa de la vivienda justa abrieron el camino y a nosotros nos corresponde llegar tan lejos como quiera la gente de la calle y nos permita la fuerza del voto de la gente. De eso van estas elecciones", ha proseguido.

El jefe del Ejecutivo ha dicho que "siempre es la misma historia" con los avances sociales: primero, movilización social, luego "el no de los de siempre" (en referencia a la derecha) y luego un "desbordamiento social" que se traduce en mayorías progresistas que consolidan los avances. Ha puesto de ejemplo las protestas por la subida de las pensiones o por el matrimonio homosexual.

" Hoy, la causa social lleva el nombre de una mujer de 87 años que falleció desahuciada y nos dijo algo muy importante para recordar", ha rememorado Sánchez, parafraseando a Maricarmen: "Que lo que yo he sufrido, no lo sufra nadie más".
sources.headline: S�nchez arranca la precampa�a con la vivienda por bandera y un aviso a PP y Vox: "Ser� un perro, pero no tengo amo"

stories.headline: Spain's left faces a deadline to settle election coalitions and candidates

sources.body:
Sin candidatos y sin coaliciones cerradas. El adelanto electoral de las generales al 29 de noviembre pone, una vez más, a la izquierda más allá del PSOE entre las cuerdas y la obliga a acordar y cerrar las coaliciones en un tiempo récord, porque el próximo viernes acaba el plazo establecido por la ley electoral. El recién constituido Frente Amplio (los partidos de la esfera de Sumar ) y Podemos dicen tender puentes para el entendimiento, pero lo cierto es que no hay sintonía en sus fórmulas. Y finalmente ya se ha despejado la incógnita de Gabriel Rufián: repetirá como cabeza de lista de ERC y no tratará finalmente de tirar del carro de una izquierda a nivel nacional en horas muy bajas.

Este está siendo el primer fin de semana de la precampaña desde que Pedro Sánchez anunciara la convocatoria de elecciones el pasado fin de semana y está sirviendo para ver las carencias en este espacio.

Mientras los principales partidos, PP y el PSOE, han sacado su artillería pesada este sábado y domingo en los mítines de Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Sánchez, en la esfera de Sumar siguen tratando de dilucidar quién será su cabeza de lista . El espacio de Más Madrid ya parece haberse decantado por la exalcaldesa de Barcelona Ada Colau (comuns).

Pese a que llevaba tiempo alejada de la política activa, ha mostrado recientemente su interés de volver a la primera línea si sumaba para este proyecto. Eso sí, ha dejado claro que Podemos debería estar en la ecuación . Y ha animado a Gabriel Rufián a que lidere Frente Amplio para "unificar la izquierda a nivel estatal". También está por ver si encabeza la lista por Barcelona o por Madrid (algo que puede causar fricciones en Más Madrid).

Su perfil destaca por varios motivos: su activismo antidesahucios en el pasado como cofundadora y portavoz de la Plataforma de Afectados por la Hipoteca (PAH) encaja a la perfección como candidata en una campaña centrada por la crisis de la vivienda a raíz del desahucio y la muerte de Maricarmen y de la enorme movilización social en las calles, con una convocatoria de huelga general en un mes.

Además, Colau es un perfil más conocido entre la población general que otros que se barajaban en este espacio, como los ministros Mónica García, Ernest Urtasun y Pablo Bustinduy . El CIS de julio, el último que preguntó al respecto, refleja que solo el 54,2% de españoles conoce a García, un 39% a Urtasun y un 33% a Bustinduy. Y que Colau sea una candidata ajena al Gobierno de coalición puede jugar a su favor teniendo en cuenta que la crisis de la vivienda sigue siendo el tema que más preocupa a los españoles pese a los ocho años de Gobierno de coalición.

Sin embargo, la decisión final sobre los candidatos va más allá de Más Madrid y los comunes en un espacio que también integran Movimiento Sumar e Izquierda Unida.

Sumar ha propuesto ya a su coordinadora Verónica Martínez Barbero para liderar a la formación dentro de Frente Amplio. También IU celebra hasta el próximo miércoles sus primarias para elegir entre el andaluz Toni Valero y el extremeño Santiago Moreno su candidato dentro de la coalición. Aún así, la formación ve con buenos ojos una candidata de consenso entre todo el espacio de Frente Amplio como pueda ser Colau.
sources.headline: Las izquierdas, abocadas a otra carrera contra reloj para fijar sus coaliciones y candidatos a las elecciones generales

sources.body:
Gabriel Rufián ha deshojado la margarita y quiere volver a liderar ERC en el Congreso . Después de varios días de tensión interna y de conversaciones sobre las condiciones de su continuidad, ha decidido dar el paso que, según explican fuentes de la formación republicana, se formalizará esta tarde en una reunión de la Ejecutiva Nacional del partido donde dos tercios deben avalar a Rufián, dado que no ha presentado los avales para concurrir a las primarias del partido. Además, apuntan a que está muy cerca un acuerdo con Podemos para colaborar de cara a los comicios del 29-N y mantienen abierta la puerta a otras formaciones.

"Quiero representar a ERC y lo estoy intentando hacer con unas mínimas condiciones para poder enfrentarnos con suficientes garantías y arrestos a lo que viene", escribió en X el jueves, tras conocerse que ERC situaba com alternativa al diputado Jordi Albert para la candidatura.

La decisión llega tras abrir públicamente un periodo de reflexión sobre su futuro político y advertir de que no estaba dispuesto a repetir a cambio de nada . El adelanto electoral precipitó un debate que llevaba meses sobre la mesa, coincidiendo con su apuesta por articular un frente amplio de izquierdas en el conjunto del Estado.

Ahora, tras anunciar la decisión de seguir en ERC, fuentes de su entorno aseguran que está cerca un acuerdo con Podemos y que buscarán la "colaboración entre la izquierda soberanista y española para maximizar resultados ante lo que viene". "El Frente somos nosotros y está abierto a todos", aseveran.

ERC busca ahora rebajar las tensiones y tender puentes. El presidente de ERC, Oriol Junqueras, y la secretaria general, Elisenda Alamany , han cerrado filas públicamente con él en los últimos días y lo han señalado como el " mejor candidato " para las generales, si bien sabían que debía ser él quien moviera ficha. Ahora, con su candidatura presentada, el equilibrio entre la autonomía que reclama para liderar el grupo en Madrid y el control que quiere mantener la cúpula nacional seguirá siendo uno de los asuntos por resolver si termina siendo proclamado candidato.

En las conversaciones de los últimos días, Rufián ha reclamado más capacidad para escoger al equipo que le acompañará en las listas y para intervenir en la definición de la estrategia en el Congreso. La relación con algunos diputados se ha deteriorado hasta quedar prácticamente rota y también ha habido choques públicos con Junqueras, como ocurrió a propósito de la posición del partido ante varios decretos de vivienda, cuando Rufián se desmarcó públicamente de la postura de su líder.

Su entrada en el proceso interno, por tanto, no implica que todas esas diferencias estén resueltas. En la calle Calàbria saben, además, que su elevada proyección pública complica cualquier pulso frontal. Ese factor ayuda a explicar que la cúpula haya evitado impulsar una alternativa. Junqueras y Alamany llevaban días dando prácticamente por hecho que Rufián volvería a encabezar la candidatura, aunque puertas adentro generó malestar que condicionara públicamente su continuidad a lograr determinadas garantías.
sources.headline: Rufián será el candidato de ERC a las elecciones y mantiene la puerta abierta a alianzas con otros partidos

stories.headline: Police clear Ceuta's last major migrant settlement amid continued disputes over returns and housing

sources.body:
Desalojo a primera hora de este domingo de migrantes en la antigua fábrica de Guano

En apenas dos horas el asentamiento del Guano, el último de los lugares en el litoral ceutí en el que se habían instalado grupos de personas que habían entrado en la ciudad autónoma en julio psado, ha quedado desalojado.

Pese a que algunos de los que estaban en este lugar han huido a las montañas que rodean la ciudad en cuanto la policía ha llegado al asentamiento, la inmensa mayoría de los que lo ocupaban han sido trasladados a instalaciones del Gobierno en autocares.

Los menores han sido trasladados a centros habilitados y los adultos al Centro de Atención a los Emigrantes. Muchos de estos últimos han optado o optarán por volver a Marruecos, se supone que voluntariamente, donde las autoridades marroquíes les trasladas a zonas alejadas de la frontera ceutí.

Estas operaciones de desalojo se producen a apenas 48 horas de que los reyes Felipe y Leticia lleguen a Ceuta en su primera visita oficial. Ambos pasarán todo el martes en la ciudad autónoma donde dormirán. Al día siguiente visitarán Melilla.

La operación en el Guano ha empezado cuando la Policía Nacional se ha desplegado a primera hora de este domingo en la explanada del Guano para desalojar el último gran espacio que quedaba en Ceuta.

Más de una veintena de furgones de la Unidad de Intervención Policial (UIP) han comenzado a llegar pasadas las 8 horas a la explanada. Allí acampan menos de un millar de marroquíes desde el desalojo de los asentamientos chabolistas en las playas del Trampolín y de Benítez.

Pese a estas operaciones aún centenares de personas que entraron en julio en la ciudad ellos deambulan por las calles de barriadas como El Príncipe o Los Rosales en la periferia de Ceuta y donde vive la población de mayoría musulmana.

Según las estimaciones dadas a conocer por el ministro de Administración Territorial este viernes pasado más de 11.000 personas han regresado “voluntariamente” a Marruecos a lo largo de estos dos meses.

Estos recirtnos se han acelerado en las últimas semanas con las operaciones de desmantelamiento de los asentamientos de las playas de playas de Benítez y del Trampolín se llevaron a en torno a 1.700 personas, de las cuales la inmensa mayoría (con excepción de los menores y de algunos grupos reducidos de adultos) optó por retornar a su país.

Se calculaba que solo en el Trampolín pernoctaban más de 3.500, por lo que el resto se desperdigó por la ciudad para evitar subir a esos autobuses. Muchos de ellos huyeron hacia los montes, donde continúan a día de hoy.

Los marroquíes que han huido son conscientes de que la enorme probabilidad de que sus peticiones de asilo sean denegadas. Saben, además, que una vez reciban la denegación definitiva se enfrentarán a una orden de expulsión de España por 5 años.

Es por ello que muchos prefieren regresar de manera voluntaria a Marruecos, porque conservan la aspiración de regresar en un futuro. Otros, permanecen escondidos en la ciudad sin plantearse ni la opción de retornar ni la ser filiados para después pedir asilo. Según las fuentes policiales, estos últimos albergan la esperanza de tener una oportunidad de cruzar irregularmente a la península.
sources.headline: Culmina el desalojo del último gran asentamiento de migrantes en Ceuta

sources.body:
Abdelá Mustafa, de 26 años, preside la Asociación de Vecinos de Sidi Embarek, en Ceuta. Barrendero a tiempo parcial y cocinero de profesión en un colegio de niños con discapacidad, fue criado junto a siete hermanos por su madre, Karima, de quien aprendió valores de justicia y generosidad. Ante la reciente crisis migratoria, Abdelá se convirtió en un pilar vecinal al impulsar un campamento comunitario para proteger a mujeres y menores vulnerables.

Nos cita en el barrio de El Príncipe donde vive de alquiler porque en su barrio de Sidi Embarek los precios se han disparado y apenas hay oferta. "Mi madre sigue viviendo allí, pero la verdad es que en El Príncipe tengo a casi toda mi familia", confiesa con una sonrisa. Unaida, su mujer, atiende por la ventana abierta del salón -viven en un bajo de la zona de El Ángulo- a los inmigrantes que vienen a pedir que les carguen el móvil, que les den algo de agua o cualquier cosa para comer.

— P: En los primeros días de agosto, la llegada masiva de personas desbordó Ceuta. ¿Cómo vivió el barrio ese primer impacto y qué le impulsó a actuar de inmediato para proteger a las personas más vulnerables?

— R: Fue una emergencia que nos tocó directamente el corazón. Vimos a muchísima gente desorientada en las calles, pero lo que realmente nos conmovió e indignó fue la desprotección de las mujeres y las niñas. Me encontré con un grupo de quince mujeres que lloraban porque les habían estafado tres mil euros con un alquiler falso y no tenían dónde ir. Poco después, a las tres de la mañana, vi a dos niñas de catorce y quince años en una situación de grave riesgo e indefensión. Comprendí que no podíamos quedarnos de brazos cruzados mientras había mujeres y menores sufriendo en la calle o expuestas a peligros en los montes. Abrimos la cancha de fútbol del barrio para darles refugio. En solo veinticuatro horas pasamos de acoger a veinte personas a tener a ciento noventa y cinco, y pronto superamos las trescientas personas. Ante semejante volumen, contacté con vecinos de El Príncipe, como Hafida, para que habilitaran otro espacio comunitario y dar abasto entre todos.

— P: Crear un espacio de acogida de la noche a la mañana requiere una enorme logística. ¿Cómo se organizaron las familias para garantizar el sustento sin contar con financiación pública directa?

— R: La respuesta comunitaria fue maravillosa. Los vecinos de Sidi Embarek y de toda la periferia se volcaron desde el primer minuto con lo que tenían. Traían a la pista deportiva agua, hielo, comida, mantas, ropa y productos de higiene. Familias muy humildes hacían verdaderos malabares en sus casas; una vecina, con el único sueldo de su marido, preparaba cada día trescientos bocadillos en su cocina para repartirlos. Lo más relevante es que no recibimos ninguna ayuda económica directa de las administraciones públicas ni aceptamos donaciones en dinero. Todo lo que mantuvimos durante dos meses fue fruto del trabajo voluntario, el compromiso social y la solidaridad directa de la ciudadanía.
sources.headline: Abdel� Mustafa y la Ceuta solidaria: "Sin ayuda oficial, los vecinos abrieron sus puertas para no dejar a nadie en la calle"

stories.headline: Barcelona housing encampment in Plaça de Catalunya grows as organizers seek a general strike

sources.body: L’acampada de la plaça de Catalunya pel dret a l’habitatge ha decidit protegir l’espai amb tanques al perímetre. “Vam rebre amenaces feixistes. Està barrat per autoprotecció” , ha declarat Kiara Monrroy, membre de l’acampada, qui ha especificat que “ la gent pot passar , no s’està tancant la porta a ningú”. Ara bé, ha advertit que si algú exhibeix comportaments que vagin en contra de l’acampada, demanaran “que abandoni el recinte”. De fet, en els darrers dies, alguns acampats han dit que s’havien detectat alguns infiltrats . Una acampada autoorganitzada L’acampada va començar amb quatre tendes de campanya i 24 persones, però segons Monrroy aquest dissabte ja hi ha aplegades més de 625 tendes, amb unes 825 persones . Assegura que són una barreja d’associacions i persones que, individualment, han decidit sumar-s’hi. Després de més de 10 dies, explica que ja és tot un “grup autoorganitzat de classe treballadora i estudiants” en què hi ha comissions, una cuina i infermeria i estan preparant una jornada amb activitats lúdiques . L’objectiu: la vaga general Per tot plegat, Kiara Monrroy considera que han demostrat “que l’horitzontalitat sense jerarquia és possible” i reivindica que no han “necessitat suport ni reforç policials” , sinó que tot ho han “gestionat de manera interna”. Per acabar, ha reiterat que l’objectiu comú segueix sent trobar el consens per anar a “la vaga general per un habitatge digne”. També et pot interessar El Sindicat de Llogateres deixa l’acampada de Catalunya per centrar-se en la vaga general de l’11-N Francis Manzano Rojas 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: L’acampada de la plaça de Catalunya per l’habitatge, protegida amb tanques per “amenaces feixistes”

stories.headline: Poblenou group says the 22@ redevelopment has failed to deliver promised affordable housing

sources.body: Quan l’any 2000 es va aprovar el pla urbanístic del 22@ , que afecta en bona part el barri del Poblenou , l’objectiu era enderrocar els edificis industrials i substituir-los majoritàriament per empreses. Tot i això, es va aconseguir reservar un 10 % del sòl per a habitatge protegit . En aquell moment això representava que s’hi podrien fer uns 4.000 habitatges. 22 anys més tard, es va fer una modificació del PGM que va ampliar la xifra fins als 15.000 pisos protegits . El 2026, però, només s’han construït uns 1.800 habitatges a preus assequibles tot i que al barri hi ha una vintena de solars públics que estan buits de mitjana des de fa 10 anys. En aquests terrenys s’hi podrien construir uns 2.000 pisos. Falten 100 anys per acabar el 22@ Aquestes són les dades que ha recollit l’ Observatori dels Barris del Poblenou , entitat que considera que “ el 22@ és un model fallit “, segons explica a l’ Infobarris l’Albert València, arquitecte urbanista i membre de l’entitat. “Actualment, només el 30 % del 22@ s’ha construït “, ho justifica. I afegeix: “Si se segueix construint al ritme dels primers 26 anys, encara trigarem un segle a acabar el 22@”. De fet, al barri es pot veure que encara hi ha moltes naus industrials o amb altres activitats que queden al marge dels usos previstos. Per construir habitatge protegit al 22@ es van preveure dos mecanismes diferents. Per una banda, quan s’han fet grans transformacions urbanístiques per construir oficines, el promotor ha hagut de donar una part del sòl a l’Ajuntament per fer-hi habitatge protegit . Cessió de sòl públic Aquest és el cas de l’illa compresa entre els carrers de Badajoz, Almogàvers, Ciutat de Granada i Pere IV. Aquí s’està construint el bloc de la cooperativa Abril , que es preveu acabar properament i traslladar-s’hi a finals d’any. Al costat, en canvi, hi ha un dels solars buits de propietat municipal que es van cedir a l’Incasòl i on, per ara, no s’ha començat a construir. “Aquí veiem quines decisions són encertades i quines no a l’hora de promoure habitatge protegit: quan se cedeix sòl cooperatives d’habitatge, com que són els mateixos usuaris els interessats a solucionar la necessitat d’habitatge, van més ràpid que un promotor amb ànim de lucre “, reflexiona l’Albert València. Un 70 % d’habitatge protegit en les grans reformes València explica que l’altre mecanisme per aconseguir habitatge assequible previst pel projecte del 22@ són les grans rehabilitacions de finques on ja hi ha habitatges : si en el conjunt de la ciutat en aquests casos cal que la reserva sigui d’un 30 %, a la zona del 22@ els habitatges protegits de l’immoble han de representar el 70 % del total. Tot i això, no tot és tan fàcil: “En aquest tipus de transformacions en què es genera habitatge protegit en edificis existents costa molt fer-ne la traçabilitat per saber què s’ha fet en realitat “, diu l’arquitecte. Canvis legislatius per afavorir l’habitatge protegit Amb aquestes dades l’Observatori dels Barris del Poblenou té clar que aquest és el barri amb més potencial per construir-hi habitatge assequible de tota la ciutat però per fer-ho realitat caldria “posar al centre les necessitats del veïnat i el dret a l’habitatge, en lloc de l’actual model especulatiu basat en la generació d’oficines i la projecció internacional”, opina l’Albert València, que assegura que si hi ha voluntat política es podria tornar a modificar el PGM del 22@ o, fins i tot, es podrien promoure canvis legislatius que afavorissin que els sòls reservats per a oficines es poguessin utilitzar per fer-hi habitatge protegit. 3.000 places de residències en 20 anys En canvi, des que es va aprovar el 22@ sí que s’hi han construit residències d’estudiants , concretament unes 3.300 places. La majoria d’habitacions es lloguen a preus elevats i les solen ocupar joves de països rics i amb un alt poder adquisitiu . A més, a l’estiu, quan no hi ha estudiants, també lloguen habitacions per a estades curtes, com si fossin hotels. Aquestes residències es van poder construir en sòl reservat per a oficines o d’equipaments amb molta llibertat fins que el PEUAT i la modificació del PGM del 2022 hi van posar fre . “Ara és molt difícil que es puguin construir residències d’estudiants en aquesta àrea”, explica València. Des de l’Observatori dels Barris del Poblenou aquest fre es veu amb bons ulls, ja que considera que aquest tipus d’allotjament afavoreix la gentrificació del barri . Negocis per a turistes o expats De fet, l’Observatori calcula que el preu de l’habitatge al mercat lliure del Poblenou s’ha multiplicat per dos des del 2014 i això ha tingut també un impacte important en els negocis del barri: a la rambla del Poblenou, l’any 2005 al 80 % dels locals hi havia botigues mentre que l’altre 20 % es dedicava a la restauració . Actualment, la proporció s’ha invertit. “Veiem que la majoria d’aquests negocis estan destinats a turistes o expats que viuen al barri, amb preus molt cars i gran part de la cartelleria i dels menús en anglès “, lamenta l’Albert València. Amb tot això, doncs, els propers anys seran clau per veure si el Poblenou i el 22@ acabaran convertint-se en la reserva d’habitatge assequible que es necessita per pal·liar la crisi residencial que viu la ciutat o si, en canvi, s’hi seguirà desenvolupant un model socioeconòmic que afavoreixi l’ arribada de nouvinguts amb alt poder adquisitiu que transformen profundament el tarannà del barri. Pendents d’una llei El juliol del 2026 el govern de la Generalitat i els Comuns van presentar al Parlament una proposició de llei que permetrà transformar oficines, locals comercials, hotels i aparcaments en habitatges de protecció oficial (HPO) sense necessitat de modificar prèviament el planejament urbanístic . La mesura està pensada per augmentar el parc d’habitatge assequible als municipis amb mercat tensionat, com ara el Poblenou, un fet que podria facilitar la construcció de 17.000 habitatges, segons l’Observatori dels Barris del Poblenou. La tramitació parlamentària haurà d’obtenir el suport de la majoria dels diputats del Parlament per convertir-se en llei. També et pot interessar Tres generacions que resisteixen al Poblenou: “Aquest barri és dels veïns que se l’han treballat” Francis Manzano Rojas 1 minut de lectura

stories.headline: Barcelona approves moving the remaining Marina Street cycle lane from the pavement to the roadway

sources.body: La Comissió de Govern de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha aprovat inicialment el projecte per baixar a la calçada l’única part del carril bici del carrer de la Marina que encara es troba a la vorera. Es tracta del tram de tres illes comprès entre el carrer d’Ausiàs Marc i el de la Diputació , un total de 460 metres . D’aquesta manera, es donarà continuïtat a l’eix i se’n milloraran la seguretat i la convivència amb els vianants, que guanyaran espai a la vorera. L’Ajuntament preveu destinar-hi 893.619 euros . Aspecte actual del carril bici en vorera al carrer de la Marina També et pot interessar La Barcelona ciclista: 75.000 usuaris diaris, el doble que fa 20 anys Mar Suy Saurina Marta Casals Torres 2 minuts de lectura Carril al tram central Aquest nou carril bici se situarà al tram central de la via , entre els dos sentits del trànsit rodat, i incorporarà peces separadores. D’aquesta manera, entre Diputació i Casp hi haurà quatre carrils de circulació , mentre que entre Casp i Ausiàs Marc només en quedaran tres . D’altra banda, es mantindrà un únic carril en sentit mar i entre Diputació i la Gran Via només estarà habilitat per a busos, serveis i veïns. També et pot interessar Samarretes per reclamar una via per a bicis al passeig de Maragall: “El Tour passa, el carril queda” Merche Artacho Vega 2 minuts de lectura Obres a principis d’any El projecte també preveu la instal·lació de 16 ancoratges d’aparcament per a bicicletes. Se’n reasfaltarà la calçada i se’n renovaran els semàfors i els senyals. El consistori preveu iniciar les obres durant el primer trimestre del 2027 i tindran una durada de cinc mesos .
sources.headline: L’Ajuntament completarà el carril bici en calçada al carrer de la Marina l’any 2027

sources.body:
Un ciclista en el carril bici de la calle de la Marina. / MONICA TUDELA / Bcn

El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha aprobado el proyecto para trasladar el carril bici de la calle de la Marina , en el distrito de l'Eixample, de la acera a la calzada. El tramo se encuentra entre las calles de Ausiàs Marc y Diputació y es el único de todo el eje ciclista de Marina que aún está situado sobre la acera.

El objetivo es dar continuidad a toda la red para mejorar la seguridad y funcionalidad de los trayectos en bicicleta . De este modo, la acera quedará libre para el paso de los viandantes y se mejorará el uso del espacio público, según informa el Ayuntamiento.

Asimismo, el nuevo carril bici será bidireccional y tendrá una longitud de 460 metros por sentido , dividido por piezas separadoras para evitar accidentes. La instalación del carril bici en el centro de la calzada conectará de forma continua con el tramo actual situado por debajo de Ausiàs Marc. Además, a la altura del cruce con la calle de Diputació, enlazará con la vía ciclista del lado Llobregat de Marina.

Por lo tanto, la nueva calzada quedará repartida de la siguiente manera:

El proyecto cuenta con una inversión de 893.619,46 euros, e incluye también 16 nuevos soportes para estacionar bicicletas repartidos por todo el tramo, nuevas señales y semáforos, así como la pavimentación de toda la calzada.

El Ayuntamiento contratará el servicio durante el otoño. Las obras comenzarán en el primer trimestre de 2027 y tendrán una duración prevista de cinco meses .
sources.headline: El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona aprueba trasladar de la acera a la calzada el carril bici de la calle de la Marina
